content.title: What is Inheritance?
content.description: Inheritance is an Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concept that allows one class to acquire the properties and behaviors of another class. It promotes code reusability and establishes an 'is-a' relationship between classes.

content.content: Inheritance enables a class to reuse the fields and methods of another class. The class whose members are inherited is called the parent (superclass), while the class that inherits them is called the child (subclass). Java uses the extends keyword to implement inheritance.

content.title: Why Use Inheritance?
content.content: Inheritance reduces code duplication, improves maintainability, and enables hierarchical relationships between classes.
Basic Inheritance
The child class automatically inherits accessible variables and methods from its parent class. Additional members can also be added to the child class.

content.title: Basic Inheritance Example
Parent and Child Classes
content.description: A parent class provides common functionality, while a child class extends and specializes that functionality.

content.content: The extends Keyword
The extends keyword tells Java that one class inherits from another. The subclass gains access to all non-private members of the superclass.

content.title: Using extends

content.content: Types of Inheritance
Java supports several forms of inheritance. However, it does not support multiple inheritance through classes to avoid ambiguity.

rows: Multiple child classes inherit one parent.

content.content: Single Inheritance
Multilevel Inheritance
In multilevel inheritance, one class inherits another class, which itself inherits from another class.
Hierarchical Inheritance
In hierarchical inheritance, multiple child classes inherit from the same parent class.
Method Overriding
Method overriding allows a child class to provide its own implementation of a method already defined in the parent class.

content.title: Method Overriding Example
Did You Know?
content.content: Method overriding is one of the key concepts that enables runtime polymorphism in Java.
The super Keyword
The super keyword refers to the immediate parent class. It is used to access parent constructors, methods, and variables.

content.title: Using super

content.content: Advantages of Inheritance

items.question: Code Reusability
items.answer: Common code is written once in the parent class and reused by child classes.

items.question: Maintainability
items.answer: Changes in the parent class automatically benefit child classes.

items.question: Extensibility
items.answer: New functionality can be added through subclasses.

items.question: Supports Polymorphism
items.answer: Inheritance forms the basis for runtime polymorphism.

content.content: Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Family Inheritance
content.content: A child inherits characteristics such as eye color or facial features from parents while also having unique qualities. Similarly, a child class inherits fields and methods from a parent class while adding its own features.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Inheritance, method overriding, the extends keyword, the super keyword, and different types of inheritance are among the most frequently asked Java interview topics.
Common Mistakes

items.question: Can private members be inherited?
items.answer: Private members belong only to the parent class and cannot be accessed directly by child classes.

items.question: Does Java support multiple inheritance through classes?
items.answer: No. Java supports multiple inheritance only through interfaces.

items.question: Should inheritance always be used?
items.answer: No. Use inheritance only when an 'is-a' relationship truly exists.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Inheritance allows one class to reuse another class's features. Use extends to inherit, super to access parent members, and method overriding to customize inherited behavior.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: The extends keyword creates parent-child relationships.
Java supports single, multilevel, and hierarchical inheritance.
The super keyword accesses parent class members.
